extracted.intended_audience: depositors (researchers/inventors), patent applicants and patent agents preparing biological-material deposits under the Budapest Treaty; culture-collection administrative staff
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional procedural and technical requirements for depositing microorganisms, cell lines, plasmids, viruses, etc., with culture collections under the Budapest Treaty (how to prepare, what to submit, forms, notifications, fees, and sample furnishing procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of microorganisms acceptable for deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of accepted organism types (e.g., bacteria including actinomycetes, fungi including yeasts, plasmids, bacteriophages, viruses, cell cultures, eukaryotic DNA, algae, protozoa, seeds, embryos, hybridomas) and explicit EXCEPTIONS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections enumerate accepted categories and specific exclusions: e.g., exclude microorganisms dangerous to human health or environment, those requiring special containment, mixtures of undefined/unidentifiable microorganisms, hybridomas or plant tissue cultures in some collections. Specific wording varies by collection (examples: KCTC, KCCM, VKM, NRCA, VKPM). Collections reserve the right to refuse for security reasons or when technically unable to carry out viability testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and quantity requirements (preferred preparation forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preferred physical form for deposit (e.g., lyophilized when possible; viruses and bacteriophages that cannot be lyophilized should be frozen; agar stabs acceptable in some collections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All replicates submitted should be from the same batch of lyophilized or frozen preparations. If lyophilization is not possible, submit active cultures in suitable media and consult the collection in advance. Some collections specify that bacteriophages and viruses must be frozen; others prefer agar stabs or lyophilized forms (VKM, KCTC, KCCM, VKPM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of replicates to be submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections require a minimum number of replicates/ampoules/vials of the deposit, varying by organism type and by collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: KCLRF: Cell lines in frozen form: 7. KCTC: actinomycetes/bacteria/fungi/yeasts/bacteria with plasmid: 10; plasmids/algae/protozoa/cell lines/hybridomas/viruses/bacteriophages: 25. KCCM: bacteria/fungi/yeasts/actinomycetes: 8; plasmids/bacteria with plasmids/viruses/bacteriophages: 25. VKM/NRCA: five stabs or 50 ampoules. VKPM: fungi/yeasts/bacteria/plasmids(in host): 20 lyophilized cultures or 5 agar cultures; plasmids (purified DNA): 25 vials (100 ng each); cell lines and hybridomas: 25 frozen samples; bacteriophages: 5×0.5 ml (free cell lysate) with at least 10^8 pfu/ml. Numbers differ by collection and organism type — depositor must follow the target collection's specific minima.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organism‑specific technical specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical minimum/specifications for particular organism types (e.g., bacteriophage titre, plasmid aliquot amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: bacteriophage suspensions must contain at least 10^7 pfu/ml (KCCM); some collections require at least 10^8 pfu/ml for supplied lysates (VKPM). VKPM specifies plasmid purified DNA vials of 100 ng each. Follow collection-specific technical numeric requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time required for viability testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical average lengths of time collections require to test viability for different organism categories, with caveat that some cases may take longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: KCLRF: cell lines 14 days (or up to 28 days). KCTC: bacteria 7 days (up to 14); fungi/yeasts/actinomycetes/algae/protozoa 10 days (up to 20); plasmids/viruses/cell lines/hybridomas 14 days (or up to 30). KCCM: bacteria 7 days (up to 14); fungi/yeasts/actinomycetes 10 days (up to 20); plasmids/viruses/bacteriophages/cell lines 14 days (up to 30). VKM/NRCA/VKPM provide similar ranges (examples: VKM bacteria/fungi/yeasts 7 days with longer upper bounds; NRCA bacteria 15 days (or up to 30)). Depositors should expect variability and occasional longer durations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depositor checks and renewal of stocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections prepare their own batches from depositor-supplied material and require depositors to check authenticity; collections store part of the original material and prepare new batches for distribution/renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections subculture or otherwise prepare their own distribution batches at time of deposit and as stocks diminish. Depositors are routinely asked to check authenticity of batches prepared by the collection. Collections routinely check new deposits for contamination and may return contaminated submissions to the depositor (VKM, NRCA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Official language(s) for communication with the collection (often local language with English accepted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: KCLRF/KCTC/KCCM: Korean official but correspondence may be in English. VKM/NRCA: Russian official but communications may be exchanged in English. Depositor should follow collection-specific language guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual arrangements and right to withdraw
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections generally do not enter into a written contract; completion/signing of deposit form effects administrative terms (including surrendering right to withdraw during required storage period).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wording varies: by signing the deposit form, the depositor surrenders the right to withdraw the deposit during the required storage period (KCLRF, KCTC, KCCM). Some collections explicitly state they do not enter into a written contract (VKM/NRCA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Import and quarantine requirements for overseas depositors
rubrics_metrics.description: Overseas depositors must contact the collection in advance about shipping; certain pathogens require permits and may be subject to import/quarantine regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections advise prospective depositors on permits/procedures where applicable (KCLRF, KCTC, KCCM). Some collections (e.g., VKM) state depositors must check applicable national regulations themselves and the collection does not advise on import permits. Depositors should contact the target collection well before shipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms required for original deposit and later amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory use of international model forms (or collection equivalents) for accession and for later indications/changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositors required to complete equivalent of model form BP/1 as accession form for original deposits; use BP/7 equivalent for later indication or amendment of the scientific description and/or proposed taxonomic designation. Collections refer to these model BP forms; follow the collection's local/formal equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official notifications and mandatory international forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Receipt, viability statements and other official notifications are issued on mandatory international forms (BP series) or the collection's equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common mappings: BP/4 = receipt; BP/9 = viability statement; BP/8 = attestation of receipt of later indication/amendment; BP/14 = notification of furnishing of a sample. Collections may have their own standard forms for other notifications but use the BP forms for the international paperwork.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unofficial notifications and communication options
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections may or may not provide unofficial communications (e.g., telephone notification of deposit date/accession number or viability test result) before issuing official forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some collections will telephone deposit date and accession number and communicate viability test results if requested (KCLRF, KCTC, KCCM). Others (VKM, NRCA) do not provide unofficial notifications prior to issuing the official receipt and viability statement. Check collection policy on unofficial communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply of information to a patent agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections do not routinely ask for the patent agent's details but will supply copies of receipt/viability statement to depositor or to their agent on request, with collection-specific limits on sending to both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., some collections will send copies to either the depositor or the agent if requested but not to both (KCLRF, KCTC, KCCM). Others will supply to both if requested (VKM, NRCA). Depositor must request desired distribution of official documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Converting previous non‑Budapest Treaty deposits to Budapest Treaty deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions and administrative requirements for converting earlier deposits to Budapest Treaty status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common rules: conversion permitted only if original deposit was made for patent purposes (in some collections); depositor must supply copy of previous receipt; conversions are subject to the normal storage fee levied on Budapest Treaty deposits regardless of prior fees. Some collections allow conversion even if not originally for patent purposes but then standard fees apply (VKM example). Follow target collection's conversion policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making a new deposit (BP/2 and related forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements when making a new deposit (as distinct from original deposit or conversion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depositor is required to complete model form BP/2 when making a new deposit and to supply copies of relevant documents required by Rule 6.2. Receipt and viability statement for a new deposit are issued on BP/5 and BP/9 respectively (per collection usage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing of samples—request procedure and requester responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure that third parties must follow to request samples and the responsibilities of the requesting party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections provide model request form BP/12 and/or national IPO request forms. Furnishing is on the basis that the requesting party is responsible for complying with relevant health and safety and import requirements in their jurisdiction. Collections assume overseas requesters have met their country's import requirements. All samples furnished are from batches prepared by the collection itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of the depositor when samples are furnished
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how depositors are notified when a sample of their deposit is furnished to a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many collections issue notification on BP/14 when samples are furnished (KCLRF, KCTC, KCCM, NRCA). Some collections do not notify depositors when samples are furnished (VKM). Check the collection's policy on depositor notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cataloguing of Budapest Treaty deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether Budapest Treaty deposits are listed in the collection's published catalog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several collections state they do not list Budapest Treaty deposits in their published catalog (KCLRF, KCTC, KCCM, VKM). Depositors should not expect public catalog listing unless explicitly stated by the collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule of fees and fee exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees charged by collections for services: deposit (storage for specified term), furnishing of samples, issuance of viability statements, attestations, communications; fees often exclude transport/bank charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collections provide schedules with numeric examples (e.g., KCLRF/KCTC/KCCM list fees in KRW: original deposit ~800,000–900,000 KRW, furnishing ~100,000–150,000 KRW, etc.; VKM lists USD 650 storage, USD 100 viability, USD 130 furnishing; NRCA lists USD 250 storage, USD 70 viability, etc.). Fees do not include transport costs or bank fees and may include other charges for communications/carriage. Check the exact fee schedule of the receiving collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for depositors (availability and format)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the collection provides written guidance notes or other support to prospective depositors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many collections 'do not at present produce specific written notes' but are ready to give advice by telephone or letter/email (examples: KCLRF, KCTC, KCCM, VKM, NRCA). Depositors should contact collections directly for advice.
